exceptions.reason: This chart's categories run across the plot, so the cursor answers ArrowLeft and ArrowRight and leaves the vertical pair to the page. A chart that consumed ArrowUp would take the page scroll away from a keyboard reader who only wanted to leave it, which is the same reasoning that keeps touch-action off the rail.

additions.reason: The chart plot is one keyboard region and the data cursor rides inside it: the rail carries tabindex="0", role="group" and the chart name whether it overflows or not, and the arrow keys, Home, End and Escape move a cursor that drives exactly what hover drives. The tab stop used to appear only while the rail overflowed, on the reasoning that a stop on a fitting rail would be dead; it stopped being dead the moment the region answered keys.
